newsitem.title: USA: CSCE COFFEE ENDS DOWN, BUT OFF SESSION LOWS.
newsitem.headline: CSCE COFFEE ENDS DOWN, BUT OFF SESSION LOWS.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended with pared losses on Monday, as an afternoon round of local short-covering lifted prices off session lows, dealers said.

Heavy speculative and trade selling of the nearby September/December switch kept the market under pressure for much of the day, with the spot September contract stumbling to a session low of 194.00 cents a lb, down a hefty 11.85 cents.
"It was all switches," said one trader. "They bombed it on the switches."
At the close, September stood down 6.50 cents, at 199.35 cents. Second-month December fell 3.10 cents on the day, to 174.75 cents, while the back months closed 0.75 to 1.25 cents lower.
The September/December switch shrank to 24.60 cents compared with 28.00 cents at the close on Friday. December/March 1998 narrowed to 20.00 cents versus 22.10 cents the previous session.
"The spreads have evened out," said Refco Inc analyst Ann Prendergast. "I think they got too far ahead of themselves and corrected."

Coffee prices rose at the opening, as dealers said sentiment was buoyant after prices rallied back from lows on Friday. September peaked at 209.00 cents, but its failure to breach 210.00 cents chart resistance and steady selling of the September/December switch sent prices into negative territory for the remainder of the session.
Some traders said reports of Brazil's coffee belt escaping damaging cold this past weekend and forecasts for frost-free conditions through next week weighed on the market.
Refco's Prendergast said views that roaster's near-term supply needs were met also may have dampened sentiment.
"I think what is making this market edgy is uncertainty about roasters needs," Prendergast said. "I tend to think they are covered.

"Exports are ahead of last year and there's got to be coffee around," she said. "The quality -- especially of the tail end of the exports -- may be disappointing, but you still have to wonder about consumption and what the effect of higher retail prices has had on consumption."
Prendergast noted that September's close near $2 was constructive, but said she expected the spot month to range between 194 and 210 in the near-term.
On the charts, traders said September faced support at 193.00-192.00 cents, followed by 188.00 cents. On the upside, nearby resistance was seen around 202.00 cents.
After Monday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 327 60-kg bags as of August 8, to 93,792 bags. There were 35 bags of coffee was pending grading, the exchange said.
Volume on the day reached an estimated 7,118 lots.
